channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: New US Attacks On Roads, Bridges Reported As Iran Hits Back At Gulf States
item.description: US strikes on Iran widened early on July 18 from the Strait of Hormuz hotspot to multiple sites throughout central and southern Iran, including through the use of fighter jets, while Iran continued to pound US Gulf allies, as a fragile cease-fire further tattered. New US Attacks On Roads, Bridges Reported As Iran Hits Back At Gulf States.

item.title: Singapore chefs cook up chilli crab, laksa and chicken rice for 180 diners in Peru
item.description: Keng Eng Kee Seafood's Paul and Wayne Liew, Morsels' Petrina Loh and Canchita's Daniel and Tamara Chavez recently held a collaboration dinner at Lima's La Mar by Gaston Acurio, marking the first official, large-scale showcase of Singapore food in the Peruvian capital. Singapore chefs cook up chilli crab, laksa and chicken rice for 180 diners in Peru.

item.title: Reopening Hormuz Strait Easier Than Restoring Confidence, Naval Analyst Tallis Says
item.description: With the US and Iran launching fresh strikes in the Middle East, the Strait of Hormuz is back under the spotlight. Naval strategist Joshua Tallis says restoring commercial confidence -- not military force alone -- will determine when shipping returns to normal. Reopening Hormuz Strait Easier Than Restoring Confidence, Naval Analyst Tallis Says.

item.title: Ukrainians Protest For A Second Day Over Defense Minister's Dismissal
item.description: Protests spread across Ukraine on July 17, two days after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sacked the country's popular defense minister, Mykhaylo Fedorov, in a cabinet shakeup. Fedorov had reportedly clashed with Ukraine's top military leader over the country's wartime strategy. Ukrainians Protest For A Second Day Over Defense Minister's Dismissal.

item.title: China pitches AI governance model for Global South
item.description: Broader context is China’s push to both develop its alternatives to Western AI models and to offer them to developing countries; President Xi Jinping announced that Beijing would provide “5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programmes” in the next five years China pitches AI order for Global South, stresses it ‘should not be a solo performance'. China pitches AI governance model for Global South.

item.title: Biodiversity fears as human-bred hybrid fish integrate into Philippines lake
item.description: Escaped flowerhorn cichlids are causing concern for native species and about parasites capable of infecting humansEscaped ornamental aquarium fish have integrated into a local ecosystem in the Philippines, but scientists say they may be threatening the native biodiversity of the lake. Flowerhorn cichlids – human-bred hybrid fish prized for their bright-gold colour and prominent head humps – are bel Biodiversity fears as human-bred hybrid fish integrate into Philippines lake.

item.title: Ukraine Claims New Strikes On Russian 'Shadow Fleet' Tankers
item.description: Ukraine said its drones struck 159 vessels it identifies as part of Russia’s shadow fleet during a 12‑day campaign in the Black Sea Kyiv says it has hit 159 vessels linked to Russia's so-called shadow fleet during a 12-day drone campaign in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. Ukrainian officials have said the operation is aimed at disrupting the transportation of oil and other shipments used to evade international sanctions.

item.title: UN chief calls for new diplomatic push following attacks on civilian areas
item.description: The UN Secretary-General remains deeply concerned by the continuing deadly military escalation between Iran and the United States, his spokesperson said on Friday as attacks destroyed key civilian and military infrastructure across the Gulf region. UN chief calls for new diplomatic push following attacks on civilian areas.

item.title: Emergency alert spotlights sharp hunger spike
item.description: More than 256,000 people in Djibouti – around 25 per cent of the population – are likely to face crisis or emergency level hunger over the coming months, a UN-backed global food monitoring network warned in a new report released Friday. Emergency alert spotlights sharp hunger spike.

item.title: An Alleged Russian FSB Hacker Traveled To Thailand. Now He's Facing 10 Years In A US Prison.
item.description: What’s unusual about the arrest of Denis Obrezko is how relatively rare it is for Russian hackers to be detained abroad these days. What’s also unusual: Obrezko used to work for Russia’s FSB. And it also appears he was careless. An Alleged Russian FSB Hacker Traveled To Thailand. Now He's Facing 10 Years In A US Prison.

item.title: China’s desert mock-up rehearses a US warship’s death at sea
item.description: This month, multiple media outlets reported that satellite imagery showed a detailed, full-scale replica of a US Navy Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer in China’s remote Taklamakan Desert. Construction of the 155-meter mock-up began around October 2025 at the Ruoqiang Test Range in Xinjiang and was completed within six months. item.title: India’s AI moment more about deployment than discovery
item.description: For three decades, India was the world’s back office. During the next three decades, it may become the world’s AI workshop. That possibility lies behind one of the most consequential questions facing India’s economy. item.title: US Attacks, Iran Retaliates -- But White House Insists Diplomacy Still Possible
item.description: US forces stepped up attacks on Iranian sites, reportedly striking key bridges and an airport, prompting retaliatory action by Tehran, even while the White House said talks between the warring sides were still under way and that diplomacy was still a viable option. US Attacks, Iran Retaliates -- But White House Insists Diplomacy Still Possible.

item.title: Russian Fuel Shortages Trigger Fights, Public Anger
item.description: Worsening fuel shortages are causing more frustration across Russia, with social media videos regularly showing fist fights at gas stations and drivers demanding answers from authorities. The Kremlin claims the country's energy system remains resilient. Russian Fuel Shortages Trigger Fights, Public Anger.

item.title: Iran Deal Must Put Iranians At The Center, Policy Analyst Elizabeth Kennedy Trudeau Says
item.description: As tensions between the US and Iran intensifies, with renewed military strikes and growing arguments around the Strait of Hormuz, global attention has focused on regional security, commercial shipping, and the risk of wider escalation. Iran Deal Must Put Iranians At The Center, Policy Analyst Elizabeth Kennedy Trudeau Says.

item.title: IOM warns of potential El Niño threat to families displaced by earthquake
item.description: Thousands of people remain displaced three weeks after the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and the possible formation of a strong El Niño climate pattern could worsen their already dire situation, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) warned on Thursday. IOM warns of potential El Niño threat to families displaced by earthquake.

item.title: WHO warns DR Congo Ebola outbreak is outpacing response as Uganda reaches milestone
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has become the third largest on record and is spreading faster than any previous one during the first month of exposure, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday. WHO warns DR Congo Ebola outbreak is outpacing response as Uganda reaches milestone.

item.title: Ukrainians Rally Against Dismissal Of Popular Defense Minister
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's sacking of Ukraine's popular defense minister, Mykhaylo Fedorov, is not just a dramatic shakeup of his cabinet. It's sent shock waves through the country's political and military circles, and it's driven protesters into the streets. Ukrainians Rally Against Dismissal Of Popular Defense Minister.
